mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals accommodative monetary policy, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in <50% of triggered instances during easing cycles, or the 20d returns are not statistically significantly higher than the 60-day rolling average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment claims (UNRATE) above 3.8% triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days, reflecting investor concerns about labor market weakening.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises >0.1 percentage points in one month
failure_condition: UNRATE crosses above 3.8% without subsequent negative 20d returns, or 20d returns are not significantly negative relative to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent decline in the federal funds rate and rise in GDP growth (GDPC1) signal accommodative monetary policy, amplifying equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls >0.2% while GDPC1 rises >1% in one month
failure_condition: The 60d returns are not significantly positive compared to baseline (t-test p >0.05) despite the signal, or the proxies move in opposite directions without the combined effect.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, simultaneous strength in GDP growth (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20d returns are not significantly positive in late-cycle periods, or the proxies do not show concurrent strength relative to historical late-cycle data.

mechanism_narrative: Rising labor participation rates (HOUST) signal strong job market activity, prompting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST rises without subsequent positive 5d returns, or returns are not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105.0 triggers positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days, reflecting stronger supply-side growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 105.0 in one month
failure_condition: INDPRO crosses above 105 without positive 20d returns, or returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in federal funds rate and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises >0.3% while UNRATE falls >0.1% in one month
failure_condition: The 60d returns are not significantly negative despite the signal, or the proxies move in opposite directions without the combined effect.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, rising GDP growth (GDPC1) and retail sales (HOUST) indicate economic resilience, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5d returns are not significantly positive in post-shock periods, or proxies do not show concurrent strength relative to historical post-shock data.
